newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zambia says getting budget back on track.
newsitem.headline: Zambia says getting budget back on track.

text.p: Zambia, criticised by the International Monetary Fund earlier this month for failing to meet budget targets, expects to make up the lost ground by mid-year, Finance Minister Ronald Penza said on Thursday.
Penza also told Reuters that a long-awaited Consultative Group meeting with Western donors would be held in Paris on July 9, boosting hopes of a restoration of normal bilateral aid flows.
The government failed to achieve a budget surplus in the first quarter of the year as projected in the 1997 budget, prompting the warning from the IMF.
But Penza said the "slippage", caused by liquidity problems at state mining concern Zambia Consolidiated Copper Mines (ZCCM), should soon be rectified.
"There has been a fiscal slippage in the first quarter but that we should be able to correct by the second quarter," Penza said while attending an investment conference in Harare.

Short-term financing had been arranged to deal with ZCCM's problems and longer term, the government expected a budget boost from further privatisation revenues, including cash from the sale of ZCCM assets.
The IMF said last week that Zambia had to get its budget in order before discussions on the country's second-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility could resume.
"Things should be in fairly good shape for us to continue with our programme with the Fund," Penza said.
He was confident that Zambia would soon restore normal relations with bilateral donors who cut aid after controversy surrounding last year's general elections.
Zambia badly needs their help, with one third of the country's US$1.1 billion budget for 1997 dependent on donor aid.
A key Consultative Group neeting with donors, deferred indefinitely last year in protest against the way elections were held, would now take place in Paris on July 9, he said.
